summary:
### Key Topics Discussed
- Clarification of cost surcharges, projects, teams, and invoicing.
- Definition of cost centers and projects for teams and equipment.
- Invoice references and main paradox level, specifically ER reference and invoice reference.
- Invoicing strategies and cash flow, including collective invoicing per order concept, per object, or per week.
- The conflict between immediate invoicing for cash flow and customer preference for fewer invoices/invoicing upon job completion.
- Technical implementation of invoicing, including API integration with Fortnox and the structure of invoice headers and line items.
- Our reference ("vår referens") on the order concept and invoice.
- Internal invoicing references for quick lookup of order concepts.
- Detailed breakdown of required information in the invoice header for both our reference and customer's reference, linked to the order concept.
- Dynamic reference fields that retrieve metadata from tasks, such as façade numbers, or hardcoded unique order numbers.
- Handling multiple customer invoice references for the same customer, potentially leading to multiple invoices.
- Swedish standard for two information fields in invoicing: one for name/department and another for a reference number (order or project number).
- Free-text invoice lines with a 50-character limit per line, where the performer can describe work done.
- Fixed invoice line references, similar to performer logic for a specific task, for items like "standard laundry washing" (tvätt av standardtvättkärl).
- Metadata fields for invoice line items, allowing one or more fields per line item.
- Handling text exceeding the 50-character limit for free-text invoice lines by splitting it into new lines.
- Combination of metadata fields (e.g., property number) on a single invoice line item.
- How Trivo sends article numbers (e.g., K100) to the accounting system for auto-coding and tax handling.
- Trivo's ability to send a 50-character description for article-based invoice lines, similar to free-text lines.
- Invoice line item details: quantity, unit price, and total sum sent to the accounting system.
- Fortnox handling the summation for invoices with multiple lines or pages.

### Decisions Made
- Trivo and Replici need a function to manage performers (already exists).
- Trivo and Replici need a function to manage equipment (partially exists).
- Trivo and Replici need a function to assemble a team.

### Action Items
- Add "our reference" field to the order concept.
- Ensure Trivo can handle free-text lines on invoices.
- Double-check API integration with Fortnox for correct transmission of article number, description, quantity, and unit price for invoice line items.

### Important Points & Insights
- When creating a team, it should be possible to define the cost center and project that the team represents.
- The cost center should automatically follow the equipment.
- The project should automatically follow the team.
- These are two information fields: when registering an employee, define their project, and when registering a vehicle, define its cost center.
- Cost center and project should also be linked to the article.
- Invoice references can be handled in two ways, with ER reference (e.g., person or property number) and invoice reference (e.g., a sequential number).
- These references are located at the top of the invoice header/document.
- If these are hardcoded into the unique order concept, they will automatically apply.
- All items created within an order concept that will become an invoice will be on the same invoice; the invoice can have multiple line items.
- The order concept should allow users to choose to wait for invoice creation until all tasks are completed for the entire order concept or per object, or to have a weekly collective invoice for tasks performed during that week.
- These invoicing strategies are designed to improve cash flow.
- The fundamental goal of the system is to issue invoices as quickly as possible, although customers often prefer fewer invoices and waiting until work is complete.
- Replici must understand that there are two fields next to the customer number in the invoice header.
- Trivo will send an information packet via API to Fortnox (or other accounting systems), including the customer number, to ensure the correct customer is identified for invoicing.
- The invoice header will automatically include the invoice reference and customer reference (kundens referens), along with the invoice creation date, our reference ("vår referens"), and our designation.
- The field for "our reference" on the order concept is customary in Sweden and needs to be added (e.g., the name of the Kinab employee who received the order).
- The internal invoice designation (vår fakturabetäckning) will be the order concept number to enable quick lookup of the source of an invoice by an administrator.
- The invoice header requires five pieces of information (excluding date): customer number, our reference, our invoice reference, customer's reference (from order concept), and customer's invoice reference (from order concept).
- Trivo needs a logic to understand if dynamic customer invoice references (e.g., 22 for some tasks, 23 for others) for the same customer should result in separate invoices.
- The dynamic invoice reference, e.g., 22, should be grouped under a specific category like 'M', while others are under a different category.
- The traditional Swedish standard for invoicing includes two separate information fields: one for the ordering entity (person or department who will approve the invoice) and another for a reference number (order or project number).
- In property-related work, these fields can often be dynamic, pulling information like a person's name, department name, or façade number from a hierarchy like "Svenska Bostäder" order.
- The customer number from Fortnox is crucial for directing the invoice and is the primary identifier.
- The customer's two reference fields can either be controlled by metadata or be hardcoded for the entire order concept.
- For KINAB's corresponding two reference fields, one is completely open for manual input (e.g., the KINAB employee responsible for the order).
- The other KINAB field is system-generated by Trivo, creating the order concept and linking it to tasks and ultimately the invoice.
- Trivo should be able to deliver free-text lines, up to 50 characters, where the performer can write descriptions of the work done, dynamically linked to a task and reflected on the invoice.
- Trivo should also manage fixed invoice line references, using a similar logic to how performers are assigned to tasks, for specific articles like "standard laundry washing" (tvätt av standardtvättkärl).
- Metadata fields on invoice line items should be limited to 50 characters, depending on the accounting system.
- If a description for an invoice line item exceeds 50 characters, it should be split into new lines.
- Only alphanumeric metadata fields can be handled; images cannot be included.
- Multiple metadata fields can be combined into a single 50-character invoice line if short enough (e.g., "22 Stora Boven fyra").
- When Trivo sends an article number (e.g., K100) to the accounting system, the system automatically handles accounting, VAT codes, etc.
- Trivo can also send a 50-character description for article-based invoice lines, similar to how free-text lines are handled.
- Example of an article description provided: "tvätt av kärl, standard."
- For each invoice line item, Trivo will send the article number, description, quantity, and unit price. The accounting system will then calculate the total sum for each line.
- Fortnox will handle the sum calculation for all invoice lines, even across multiple pages.

### Open Questions/Pending Items
- Next steps for defining the API flow for invoice line items.
- There should be a function to capture the ordering entity (beställning) for internal reference.
